7. The respondent No. 5 also filed Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated  15-2-2010 stating that at the time of filing of the Affidavit-in-Opposition on 28-5-2008, the respondent No. 5 could not filed the certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004. The Sonali Bank authority filed an application for obtaining certified copy of the judgment on 3-4-2005 and obtained on 10-4-2005 and, on the other hand, writ petitioner filed an application on 10-10-2005 for certified copy of the judgment and obtained the same on 17-10-2005. 

 8. The respondent No. 5 filed another Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 27-4-2010 stating further that the certified copy of the judgment passed in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 was obtained by the Manager, Sonali Bank Chandraganj Branch, Laxmipur on 10-4-2005 and accordingly attested copy of the certified copy was forwarded to the Assistant General Manager (AGM), Regional Officer, Sonali Bank Laxmipur by letter dated 11-4-2005. Then with reference to the letter of the Regional AGM Office dated 13-9-2005, Manager, Chandragonj Branch again obtained a fresh certified copy on 17-10-2005 and sent it to the Regional AGM office, Laxmipur by its letter dated 25-10-2005. After perusal of the fresh certified copy dated 17-10-2005, it transpires that the learned Special Judge, passed the judgment deleting the name of the Accused Md Shamsur Rahman and convicting the other accused Abdul Mannan and Amir Hossain Khan and accordingly Branch Manager by letter dated 27-10-2005 forwarded the fresh certified copy to the Regional AGM Office, Laxmipur. In this respect Manager, Chandragonj Branch by letter dated 28-2-2007 informed the AGM, Regional Office Laxmipur of the same and accordingly Regional Office by its letter dated 28-2-2007, addressed to the Assistant General Manager, Personnel Management Division, Head Office Dhaka informing the certified copy issued by the Special Judge Court, Noakhali on 17-10-2005 (Annexure-X(1) to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition) will be treated as judgment passed by the Special Judge Court, Noakhali in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 and not the certified copy of the judgment issued earlier by the Court on 10-4-2005 (Annexure-X to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition). 

 9. In course of hearing of the Rule, it appears to us that two judgments both dated 27-10-2009 was delivered in Special Case No. 16 of 2003 by the learned Special Judge, Noakhali. One judgment was of conviction and the other was of acquittal of the petitioner. For clarification of the matter and for proper and effective disposal of the Rule an order was passed by this Court on 18-2-2010 to transmit the entire record of Special Case No. 16 of 2003. After receipt of the case record, we have carefully and meticulously examined the entire case record. Thereafter, it transpires that only one judgment dated 24-10-2007 has been pronounced. This mistake was committed due to oversight of the earlier order dated 23-11-2002 passed by the Special Court, Laxmipur in the aforesaid Special case acquitting the petitioner but the First certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 was obtained by the Bank authority issued by the Court on 10-4-2005 did not reflect the order of the Special Court passed on 23-11-2002. 

 10. Subsequently fresh/corrected certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 was issued by the Special Judge, Noakhali in the Special Case No. 16 of 2003 on 17-10-2005 which reads as under: 

 19. It was also admitted that due to over-sight and bonafide mistake of the learned Special Judge two sets of certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 was issued, firstly on 10-4-2005 (Annexure-X to the Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition) and subsequently on 14-8-2005 (Annexure-E to the writ petition) and on 17-10-2005 (Annexure-X(1) to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition) by the Special Judge Court, Noakhali. In first set of certified copy of the judgment issued on 10-4-2005, the Accused writ petitioner, Shamsur Rahman was convicted along with two other accused; but latter on, on the prayer of the Bank authority and the accused writ petitioner, the learned Special Court, Noakhali issued the corrected certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004, on 14-8-2005 and 17-10-2005 respectively. In the judgement it was clearly noted by the Special Judge, Laxmipur by order No. 23 dated 23-11-2002 that he acquitted the petitioner of the charges leveled against him, but which was not mistakenly noted in the certified copy of the judgment issued by the Special Court on 10-4-2005. Such bonafide mistake was committed in the certified copy of the judgment issued on 10-4-2005 due to oversight of the learned Special Judge. After detecting such bonafide mistake and to remove such confusion the learned Special Jude Court easily rectify such bonafide mistake by drawing up an order in the order sheet of the sand Special Case No. 16 of 2003 before issuance of the impugned certified copy of the judgment dated 27-10-2004 issued on 14-8-2005 (Annexure-E to the writ petition) and on 1740-2005 (Annexure-X(1) to the Supplementary-Affidavit-in-Opposition). Thus it is evident from the case record that since no formal order was drawn up in this regard in the order sheet of the said Special Case such bonafide mistake was committed due to the facts and circumstances as stated above. 

 Let a copy of this judgment be transmitted to the respondent Nos.2-6 at once for information and necessary action.
